- Lane B (pij-yielding-hamster, coder/lane-b, worktree ~/pi-hacking/pij-laneB): the PRD 009 follow-up PR (s04: refusal pointers + the first turn's type section trimmed to one line + docs pointer + the role's own rule changes, option B per req-06; the pods page only if 008 is on main).

- Open with Jordan: the authority-vs-label question (#344 parrot item 1, req-05); the binder home rule (claude_bind.rs:168); the delivered auto-release case.

Lessons:
- Disk: one cold cargo build regrows target/debug ~12 GB, so every PR hits the 25 GB shared-build floor. Never lower it; ask the prime to clear target/debug (with Jordan's ok) per PR. The coder does docs/plans/TS while waiting. CI's rust-test stands in for local cargo when blocked.
- Reviewers must be told the disk state: if shared-build refuses, they review from source and CI and NAME the mutants they couldn't run. Then the author runs the essential one.
- Cold seats: the wake price grows with context (424k idle 28 h = "price unknown"). For new work spawn a fresh coder (Copilot claude-opus-5.5 --effort medium; verify the argv, since the footer's trailing 'xhigh' is noise) and put the old seat's diagnosis in the packet.
- `pij send --fyi` refuses anything that reads as actionable (PR numbers, 'ready for your look'). For a cold advisory seat (parrot), skip the notice rather than force a wake.
- Each reviewer closes after its one round: ask for a memory note, then close + kill-pane + verify pids. Seats you forget block pr-freeze --prune (it found meerkat).
- Coders compact after each PR (Jordan): memory note first, then let the pij-bg memory turn run at a pause, after any in-flight cargo test finishes.
- Test fixtures can leak processes with ppid 1 (shared-build.test.ts's HANG fixture). Have the owning coder kill them by exact pid; that's now #350's fix.
- Heredoc + $(...) + ${..} in one bash call can trip the shell guard. Write packets with the create tool, then `pij send --body-file`.
